weeks.title: Scientific Foundations & Measurement
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: course orientation, atmosphere as a physical system, SI units, metadata and observation quality.
weeks.mathematics: Math: functions, graphs, units and dimensional reasoning.
weeks.data: Data: notebook setup, variables, tables and plotting.
weeks.communication: Communication: distinguish observation, interpretation, forecast and warning.
weeks.lab: Lab: establish a personal weather station protocol and collect a baseline dataset.

weeks.title: Atmospheric Composition, Pressure & Density
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: composition, vertical structure, pressure and density.
weeks.mathematics: Math: limits and rates of change.
weeks.data: Data: import, clean and visualize temperature/pressure records.
weeks.communication: Communication: write a source-labeled observation summary.
weeks.lab: Lab: graph pressure/density with altitude from a supplied standard-atmosphere dataset.

weeks.title: Temperature, Heat & Energy
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: temperature scales, heat, heat capacity and weather relevance.
weeks.mathematics: Math: derivative concept and instantaneous rate of change.
weeks.data: Data: calculate daily maxima, minima, range and rate of temperature change.
weeks.communication: Communication: explain temperature versus heat without oversimplifying.
weeks.lab: Lab: compare heating/cooling rates of contrasting surfaces.

weeks.title: Solar Radiation & Surface Heating
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: solar geometry, absorption, reflection and surface-energy concepts.
weeks.physics: Physics: Newton's laws and force diagrams.
weeks.data: Data: plot irradiance/temperature relationships.
weeks.communication: Communication: produce a concise solar-heating explainer.
weeks.lab: Lab: lamp/globe or surface-albedo heating investigation.

weeks.title: Surface Energy Balance
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: sensible heat, latent heat, ground heat and radiative balance.
weeks.physics: Physics: work, kinetic energy and potential energy.
weeks.data: Data: calculate and graph simplified energy-budget terms.
weeks.communication: Communication: construct an evidence-based diagram with caption.
weeks.lab: Lab: simplified daytime surface-energy budget.

weeks.title: UNIT I CHECKPOINT — Measurement, Energy & Core Mathematics
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: cumulative review Weeks 1–5.
weeks.physics: Physics: measurement, motion, forces and energy review.
weeks.data: Data: reproducibility and data-quality audit.
weeks.communication: Communication: five-minute technical briefing.
weeks.lab: Lab: integrated energy-and-observation practical. Unit checkpoint ≥80% required.

weeks.title: Water Vapor & Humidity
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: vapor pressure, relative humidity, dew point and moisture variables.
weeks.mathematics: Math: implicit rates and related rates.
weeks.data: Data: calculate dew-point depression and compare humidity metrics.
weeks.communication: Communication: explain why relative humidity changes with temperature.
weeks.lab: Lab: humidity/evaporation comparison under two environments.

weeks.title: Saturation, Condensation & Clouds
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: saturation, condensation nuclei, cloud-base formation and cloud families.
weeks.physics: Physics: circular motion and rotation introduction.
weeks.data: Data: cloud observations and categorical frequency analysis.
weeks.communication: Communication: cloud identification briefing using evidence rather than appearance alone.
weeks.lab: Lab: controlled condensation/cloud demonstration and cloud observation log.

weeks.title: SEMESTER MIDTERM I
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: midterm assessment of Weeks 1–8.
weeks.data: Data: practical data-cleaning and graphing assessment.
weeks.communication: Communication: oral defense of one laboratory result.
weeks.lab: Lab: integrated midterm practical. Every strand ≥80% required.

weeks.title: Pressure Gradients & Wind
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: pressure-gradient force and wind initiation.
weeks.data: Data: contour spacing and gradient comparison.
weeks.communication: Communication: explain why pressure maps can imply wind without claiming pressure alone determines actual wind.
weeks.lab: Lab: pressure-map gradient analysis and wind comparison.

weeks.title: Coriolis Effect & Large-Scale Flow
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: rotating reference frames, Coriolis effect and latitude dependence.
weeks.mathematics: Math: definite integrals and area accumulation.
weeks.physics: Physics: rotational motion and angular momentum.
weeks.data: Data: vector-direction plotting.
weeks.communication: Communication: correct common Coriolis misconceptions.
weeks.lab: Lab: rotating-platform or rotating-paper trajectory model.

weeks.title: UNIT II CHECKPOINT — Moisture, Clouds & Atmospheric Forces
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: cumulative review Weeks 7–11.
weeks.mathematics: Math: derivative applications plus introductory integration.
weeks.data: Data: combined moisture/wind analysis.
weeks.communication: Communication: public explainer plus technical appendix.
weeks.lab: Lab: integrated force/moisture practical. Unit checkpoint ≥80% required.

weeks.title: Friction, Boundary Layer & Local Winds
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: friction, turbulent mixing, sea/land breezes and terrain circulations.
weeks.mathematics: Math: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus concept.
weeks.physics: Physics: fluids, pressure and buoyancy introduction.
weeks.data: Data: compare coastal/inland temperature and wind records.
weeks.communication: Communication: create a local-wind forecast narrative.
weeks.lab: Lab: land-water differential-heating circulation model.

weeks.title: Air Masses & Fronts
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: source regions, modification and frontal boundaries.
weeks.mathematics: Math: accumulation and meteorological rate problems.
weeks.data: Data: map temperature/dew-point gradients.
weeks.communication: Communication: write a frontal-passage briefing with timing uncertainty.
weeks.lab: Lab: identify air masses/fronts from a station dataset.

weeks.title: Cyclones, Anticyclones & Weather Systems
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: pressure-system structure, circulation and basic midlatitude cyclone evolution.
weeks.physics: Physics: fluid dynamics concepts and Bernoulli limitations.
weeks.data: Data: track pressure-center motion.
weeks.communication: Communication: one-page storm-system analysis.
weeks.lab: Lab: sequence and annotate a developing cyclone.

weeks.title: Weather Observations & Instrumentation
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: thermometer, barometer, hygrometer, anemometer, precipitation gauges and siting.
weeks.mathematics: Math: quantitative error and percent difference.
weeks.physics: Physics: calibration, sensor response and experimental error.
weeks.data: Data: quality-control rules and outlier review.
weeks.communication: Communication: instrument-method section written in formal scientific style.
weeks.lab: Lab: instrument comparison/calibration practical.

weeks.title: Station Models, Weather Maps & First Forecast
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: station plots, map analysis, fronts and basic short-range forecasting.
weeks.data: Data: build a small surface-analysis dataset.
weeks.communication: Communication: first 3-minute operational/broadcast forecast plus written technical forecast.
weeks.lab: Lab: analyze a surface map and verify a 12–24 hour forecast.

weeks.title: SEMESTER I FINAL & PORTFOLIO DEFENSE
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: comprehensive Semester I final.
weeks.data: Data: reproducible weather-data practical.
weeks.communication: Communication: portfolio presentation and oral examination.
weeks.lab: Lab: integrated forecast-and-analysis final practical. Semester completion requires every course strand ≥80%.

courses.title: Foundations of Atmospheric Science I
courses.description: Atmospheric composition and structure; weather observation; temperature; pressure; moisture; clouds; forces; winds; air masses; fronts; cyclone structure; forecast fundamentals.

courses.title: Calculus I for Atmospheric Science
courses.description: Functions, limits, derivatives, applications of derivatives, introductory integration, rates of change, optimization, graph interpretation and meteorological applications.

courses.title: University Physics I for Atmospheric Science
courses.description: Measurement, vectors, kinematics, Newtonian mechanics, work/energy, momentum, rotation, gravitation, fluids, temperature and introductory thermodynamics.

courses.title: Scientific Programming & Weather Data I
courses.description: Python-style scientific reasoning, variables, control flow, functions, tables, CSV data, plotting, data cleaning, reproducible notebooks and basic numerical methods.

courses.title: Meteorological Communication I
courses.description: Scientific writing, source discipline, weather terminology, briefing structure, audience adaptation, uncertainty language, visual communication and oral presentation.

weeks.title: Gas Laws & Atmospheric State
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: ideal-gas relationships and equation-of-state reasoning.
weeks.mathematics: Math: integration techniques review and substitution.
weeks.data: Data: calculate state-variable relationships from atmospheric samples.
weeks.communication: Communication: write assumptions and units explicitly.
weeks.lab: Lab: pressure-volume-temperature investigation using safe apparatus or supplied data.

weeks.title: Hydrostatic Balance
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: vertical pressure decrease, gravity and density.
weeks.mathematics: Math: integration applications and differential-equation intuition.
weeks.physics: Physics: waves, frequency, wavelength and phase.
weeks.data: Data: pressure-versus-altitude numerical analysis.
weeks.communication: Communication: technical derivation narrative in plain language.
weeks.lab: Lab: compare observed/standard pressure profiles.

weeks.title: Dry Adiabatic Processes
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: parcel expansion/compression and dry adiabatic temperature change.
weeks.data: Data: plot parcel/environment profiles.
weeks.communication: Communication: explain adiabatic cooling without saying rising air 'gets farther from the Sun'.
weeks.lab: Lab: pressure-change parcel model.

weeks.title: Moist Adiabatic Processes & Latent Heat
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: condensation, latent heating and moist adiabatic behavior.
weeks.data: Data: compare dry/moist parcel traces.
weeks.communication: Communication: structured thermodynamic explanation.
weeks.lab: Lab: model dry versus saturated ascent.

weeks.title: Atmospheric Stability
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: environmental lapse rate, parcel buoyancy, stable/unstable/conditionally unstable layers.
weeks.data: Data: analyze simplified sounding profiles.
weeks.communication: Communication: confidence statement tied to vertical-profile evidence.
weeks.lab: Lab: classify stability from multiple soundings.

weeks.title: UNIT III CHECKPOINT — Thermodynamics & Stability
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: cumulative Weeks 19–23.
weeks.data: Data: sounding-analysis practical.
weeks.communication: Communication: oral thermodynamics defense.
weeks.lab: Lab: integrated parcel/stability practical. Unit checkpoint ≥80% required.

weeks.title: Cloud Microphysics
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: aerosol nuclei, droplet growth, collision-coalescence and ice processes.
weeks.mathematics: Math: vector magnitude/direction and introductory multivariable thinking.
weeks.data: Data: classify particle-growth scenarios.
weeks.communication: Communication: scientific-process diagram and caption.
weeks.lab: Lab: microphysics model or particle-growth simulation.

weeks.title: Precipitation Physics
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: precipitation growth plus melting/refreezing layers.
weeks.physics: Physics: magnetism and forces on moving charges.
weeks.data: Data: diagnose precipitation type from vertical temperature profiles.
weeks.communication: Communication: communicate uncertainty near transition zones.
weeks.lab: Lab: precipitation-type forecast practical.

weeks.title: SEMESTER MIDTERM II
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: cumulative Semester II midterm.
weeks.data: Data: statistics and sounding practical.
weeks.communication: Communication: oral scientific briefing.
weeks.lab: Lab: integrated midterm case. Every strand ≥80% required.

weeks.title: Upper-Air Observations & Soundings
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: radiosondes, pressure levels, inversions, moisture and wind profiles.
weeks.mathematics: Math: vector applications and introduction to partial rates of change.
weeks.data: Data: sounding tables, profiles and layer diagnostics.
weeks.communication: Communication: upper-air diagnostic memo.
weeks.lab: Lab: full sounding interpretation.

weeks.title: Radar Fundamentals
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: electromagnetic scattering, reflectivity and sampling limitations.
weeks.mathematics: Math: quantitative scaling and logarithmic-style interpretation where appropriate.
weeks.data: Data: spatial radar-image interpretation.
weeks.communication: Communication: distinguish radar observation from warning and forecast.
weeks.lab: Lab: track precipitation/storm motion from sequential radar frames.

weeks.title: Doppler Radar & Severe-Weather Signatures
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: radial velocity, convergence, divergence and rotation concepts.
weeks.data: Data: paired reflectivity/velocity analysis.
weeks.communication: Communication: cautious hazard-language practice.
weeks.lab: Lab: simplified Doppler velocity-signature case.

weeks.title: Satellite Remote Sensing
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: visible, infrared and water-vapor channels; geostationary versus polar perspectives.
weeks.mathematics: Math: functions of multiple variables introduction.
weeks.data: Data: compare multi-channel imagery.
weeks.communication: Communication: write what each channel supports and does not support.
weeks.lab: Lab: multispectral cloud/storm interpretation.

weeks.title: Numerical Weather Prediction Introduction
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: model grids, initial conditions, forecast equations concept, parameterization and resolution.
weeks.mathematics: Math: numerical approximation and slope/integration error ideas.
weeks.physics: Physics: computational modeling as approximation of physical laws.
weeks.data: Data: simple grid/advection experiment.
weeks.communication: Communication: explain model guidance versus official forecast.
weeks.lab: Lab: paper or code-based toy forecast model.

weeks.title: Probability, Ensembles & Forecast Uncertainty
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: deterministic versus probabilistic prediction and ensemble spread.
weeks.data: Data: ensemble mean, median, range, percentile and threshold probability.
weeks.communication: Communication: express probability without false certainty.
weeks.lab: Lab: ensemble forecast analysis.

weeks.title: Forecast Verification & Climate Data Foundations
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: hits, misses, false alarms, temperature error, bias; weather versus climate datasets.
weeks.physics: Physics: experimental validation and model comparison.
weeks.data: Data: calculate MAE, bias and simple categorical scores; compare daily record to climate normal.
weeks.communication: Communication: write a verification report that does not cherry-pick.
weeks.lab: Lab: verify a forecast set and summarize a climate baseline.

weeks.title: Three-Career Applied Studio
weeks.atmospheric_science: Operational: produce a short operational forecast package from radar/satellite/model data.
weeks.mathematics: Broadcast: turn the same technical analysis into a 2–3 minute public-facing weather segment.
weeks.physics: Climatology: analyze a multi-year weather/climate dataset and distinguish variability from longer-term pattern.
weeks.data: Data: all students document reproducible calculations and sources.
weeks.communication: Communication: audience-specific versions of one evidence base.
weeks.lab: Lab: three-station career rotation with mentor evaluation.

weeks.title: YEAR I COMPREHENSIVE FINAL, ORAL DEFENSE & ADVANCEMENT REVIEW
weeks.atmospheric_science: Atmosphere: cumulative Year I examination spanning observation, thermodynamics, forces, clouds, maps, radar, satellite, models and climate foundations.
weeks.data: Data: reproducible analysis practical with statistics/probability.
weeks.communication: Communication: oral defense before mentor/teacher panel.
weeks.lab: Lab: integrated meteorological case. Advancement to Year II requires ≥80% on every required final, practical and portfolio competency.

courses.title: Atmospheric Thermodynamics & Cloud Physics
courses.description: Gas laws, hydrostatic balance, moisture variables, saturation, adiabatic processes, stability, cloud formation, microphysics, precipitation and thermodynamic diagrams.

courses.title: Calculus II & Vector Methods for Atmospheric Science
courses.description: Integration techniques, differential equations introduction, sequences/series foundations, parametric ideas, vectors, partial-derivative introduction and meteorological applications.

courses.title: University Physics II for Atmospheric Science
courses.description: Oscillations, waves, sound, electricity, magnetism, optics, electromagnetic radiation and measurement concepts supporting radar, satellite and atmospheric remote sensing.

courses.title: Observations, Synoptic Analysis & Remote Sensing I
courses.description: Station models, METAR-style observations, surface and upper-air maps, radiosondes, radar fundamentals, satellite channels, forecast analysis and verification.

courses.title: Weather Statistics & Scientific Data II
courses.description: Descriptive statistics, distributions, probability, error, bias, correlation, regression foundations, uncertainty and ensemble interpretation.

courses.title: Forecast Communication & Professional Practice I
courses.description: Forecast writing, public-safety communication, broadcast-style explanations, technical climate summaries, ethics and source labeling.
